ai_technology: Decision trees, support-vector machines and kernel logistic regression; Bayesian hyperparameter optimization

evidence.ai_role: Learned decision trees selected compression level as an informative split; SVM and kernel-logistic classifiers tested whether dynamic cord-motion measurements add information to static MRI features for severity classification.
evidence.tested: A 90-patient training set and 22-patient internal test set were formed from 112 patients. In the 75-patient training subgroup without maximum compression at C3/4, adding motion improved repeated cross-validated accuracy from 69.6% to 73.7% (p=0.0059); the final internal test comparison gained one correct classification.
evidence.unknown: A small, single-center and imbalanced cohort with data-driven model selection remains vulnerable to overfitting. The 15-patient C3/4 training subgroup was too small for the motion-feature comparison. No external validation, causal interaction, longitudinal prognosis or treatment utility was established; acquisition and physiological confounding limit generalization.

organization: Balgrist University Hospital; University of Zurich

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full article: MRI and classifier Methods, feature ranking, subgroup and internal-test Results, Discussion and limitations; publisher publication date and Crossref online date. Supplement not independently audited.

summary: A November 23, 2026 study analyzed MRI measurements from 112 patients with degenerative cervical myelopathy. Learned hierarchical classifiers identified compression at C3/4 as a severity-associated feature. In the larger training subgroup with compression elsewhere, adding spinal cord motion improved cross-validated severity classification accuracy from 69.6% to 73.7%. Internal testing on 22 patients produced one additional correct classification. This single-center result supports a limited diagnostic association, without establishing causation, future disease progression or treatment benefit.
title: Learned MRI models link cord motion and compression level to myelopathy severity
